content: 1. Drospirenone/estradiol should be administered as one tablet orally per day. Use the lowest effective dose that adequately controls symptoms. Hormone replacement therapy is contraindicated in women with an intact uterus. This combination is indicated for the treatment of menopause-associated hot flashes and vulvar/vaginal atrophy. The safety and efficacy of this therapy have not been fully established. 2. Amiloride and drospirenone both increase serum potassium levels. Their combined use is contraindicated due to the risk of hyperkalemia, as they enhance each other's effects through pharmacodynamic synergism. 3. Belzutifan decreases the levels or effects of drospirenone by inducing hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or consider alternative drugs. Additionally, belzutifan may reduce the efficacy of hormonal contraceptives, leading to contraceptive failure or increased breakthrough bleeding. Women of reproductive potential should use effective nonhormonal contraception. Based on animal studies, belzutifan may cause fetal harm. 4. Calaspargase pegol and drospirenone interaction is of unknown mechanism. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. Due to potential indirect interactions with oral contraceptives, concomitant use is not recommended. Women of childbearing potential should use non-oral contraceptive methods. 5. Drospirenone and eplerenone both increase serum potassium levels through pharmacodynamic synergism. Their combined use is contraindicated due to the risk of hyperkalemia. 6. Drospirenone increases the levels or effects of fedratinib. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. The interaction between fedratinib (a CYP3A4 and CYP2C19 substrate) and dual CYP3A4/CYP2C19 inhibitors has not been studied. 7. Isavuconazonium sulfate increases the levels or effects of drospirenone by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. 8. Mavacamten decreases the levels or effects of drospirenone by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. Mavacamten may also reduce systemic exposure to ethinyl estradiol and progestin, potentially leading to contraceptive failure or increased breakthrough bleeding. Patients should use a contraceptive method unaffected by CYP450 enzyme induction (e.g., intrauterine system) or add nonhormonal contraception (e.g., condoms) during coadministration and for four months after the last mavacamten dose. 9. Omaveloxolone decreases the levels or effects of drospirenone by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. Omaveloxolone may reduce the efficacy of hormonal contraceptives (e.g., pill, patch, ring, implants, progestin-only pills) due to weak CYP3A4 induction. 10. Drospirenone and potassium acid phosphate both increase serum potassium levels. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. 11. Repotrectinib decreases the levels or effects of drospirenone by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. Repotrectinib, as a CYP3A4 inducer, may reduce progestin or estrogen exposure, potentially reducing the effectiveness of hormonal contraceptives. Women should use effective nonhormonal contraception. 15. Drospirenone and spironolactone both increase serum potassium levels through pharmacodynamic synergism. Their combined use is contraindicated due to the risk of hyperkalemia. 16. Tovorafenib decreases the levels or effects of drospirenone by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. If unavoidable, use additional effective nonhormonal contraception during coadministration and for 28 days after discontinuation. 17.
